s00001Mr Low Wu Yang Andreasked the Minister for National Development given that HDB announced housing plans for Gillman Barracks and Sunset Way on the same day consultation opened (a) which parameters remain open to change, including footprint, yield, retained areas, heritage and mitigation; (b) whether site clearance or tender awards will await feedback; and (c) whether HDB will publish its response before approving final plans or tenders.
s00002Miss Rachel Ongasked the Minister for National Development (a) whether alternative sites for housing were evaluated as alternatives to Gillman Barracks; (b) whether smaller-footprint or lower-density options on the Gillman Barracks site itself, with greater retention of forest cover and heritage buildings, were also assessed against the current conceptual plan; and (c) what planning considerations led to the proposed site and footprint being preferred.
Section 1Gillman Barracks impact assessment dialogue
s00003Miss Rachel Ongasked the Minister for National Development whether, after the online feedback period for the Gillman Barracks Environmental Impact Assessment and Heritage Impact Assessment closes on 6 August 2026, the Government will hold dialogue sessions with residents, heritage groups and nature groups as part of the process of refining the development plans.
s00004Miss Rachel Ongasked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the phased directional clearance plan for Gillman Barracks under the Environmental Monitoring and Management Plan will include checkpoints at which monitoring data from earlier phases is reviewed before authorising further clearance; and (b) if so, what criteria would trigger a pause or adjustment to the clearance schedule.
s00005Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdinasked the Minister for National Development in light of the recent announcement on Maju Forest (a) how has the Government's approach to balancing public housing needs with the conservation of ecologically significant forests and heat resilience evolved over the past five years; and (b) whether alternative sites, redevelopment opportunities or higher-yield development options are systematically evaluated before such locations are selected.
s00006Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdinasked the Minister for National Development with regard to proposed housing developments on former forested sites (a) what criteria are used to determine whether retained forest areas are sufficiently large and connected to remain ecologically functional over the long term; and (b) how is the effectiveness of wildlife corridors subsequently monitored.
s00007Mr Christopher de Souzaasked the Minister for National Development in light of the possible development at Maju Forest, whether the concerns and recommendations of the nature and conservation groups on preserving greenery, flora and fauna can be adopted.

s00009Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fongasked the Minister for National Development (a) how were findings from the Gillman Barracks Environmental and Heritage Impact Assessments weighed against housing needs; (b) whether alternative sites were considered; and (c) what resident engagement was conducted prior to the redevelopment announcement, including whether closed-door discussions were held and how participants were selected.
s00010Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fongasked the Minister for National Development (a) how are findings from the Maju Forest Environmental Impact Assessment taken into account in ongoing considerations for housing at Sunset Way; (b) whether alternative sites can be considered; and (c) what measures are being considered to ensure any retained ecological corridor minimises edge effects and supports wildlife movement.

s00011Ms Elysa Chenasked the Minister for National Development (a) what microclimate or urban heat-island modelling was conducted to assess the localised temperature impact of clearing forest cover at Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks; and (b) what will be the projected impact on surrounding residential areas.
s00012Ms Joan Pereiraasked the Minister for National Development regarding the Gillman Barracks redevelopment (a) what measures will be taken to ensure the preservation of its secondary hill forest and heritage buildings; (b) whether alternative brownfield sites were considered to minimise ecological impact; and (c) how public feedback from the environmental and heritage impact assessments will be incorporated into the final master plan.

s00015Ms Valerie Leeasked the Minister for National Development (a) how was public feedback gathered for the redevelopment of Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks; and (b) what other sites are being studied over the next five years for similar possible redevelopment for housing or other uses that may substantially affect existing heritage or natural areas.
s00016Mr Fadli Fawziasked the Minister for National Development in light of the recent announcement on Maju Forest (a) whether future Master Plans will refrain from zoning forested greenfield sites for development where feasible, especially where the forested sites are of ecological significance, and prioritise the redevelopment and intensifying land use on existing brownfield sites; and (b) if not, why not.

s00019Mr Alvin TanThe plans for Gillman Barracks and Sunset Way have not been finalised.
s00020Mr Alvin TanGovernment will continue to engage stakeholders, to take in views and feedback before deciding how we will carry out the development of both sites.
s00021Mr Alvin TanThis could involve adjustments to the development layout and the amount of greenery and heritage to conserve.
Section 5Public consultation on development plans
s00022Mr Alvin TanWe published the studies and conceptual plans so the public can study them, share their views and help us to shape the final development plans.
s00023Mr Alvin TanI want to assure Members that while the formal consultation period for the Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) and Heritage Impact Assessment (HIA) ends on 6 August 2026, our engagement with stakeholders will continue, as we adjust and refine the development plans based on the inputs received.
s00024Mr Alvin TanI will then explain how these principles apply to Sunset Way and Gillman Barracks.
s00025Mr Alvin TanWe also want Singaporeans and our future generations to have access to affordable public housing.
s00026Mr Alvin TanWe want hospitals, schools, and places where we can work and earn a good living.
s00027Mr Alvin TanWe want roads and public transport so we can get around.
s00028Mr Alvin TanWe also need land for defence, essential infrastructure and coastal protection.
s00029Mr Alvin TanAnd I wish we had an abundance of land, so we can provide all of these without having to make trade-offs.
s00030Mr Alvin TanOur choices are narrower than those faced by larger countries.
s00031Mr Alvin TanWe thus have to make the best use of our limited land.
s00032Mr Alvin TanThat is why we plan decades ahead, to meet Singaporeans' needs today while keeping enough options open for future generations.
s00033Mr Alvin TanHousing is one of our most pressing needs.
s00034Mr Alvin TanSome asked why housing demand continues to grow even though our total fertility rate (TFR) is lower than before.
s00035Mr Alvin TanCurrent low TFR figures reflect the smaller number of babies born in recent years.
s00036Mr Alvin TanBut Singaporeans who are buying Housing and Development Board (HDB) homes today and in the near future were born decades ago when our birth rates were higher.
s00037Mr Alvin TanAnother reason is that household sizes are getting smaller.
s00038Mr Alvin TanMore young married couples prefer a home of their own to living with their parents or extended families.
s00039Mr Alvin TanAt the same time, many prefer to live near their parents, so they can care for and support one another.
s00040Mr Alvin TanMore singles are also setting up homes of their own.
s00041Mr Alvin TanAnd more seniors now live alone or only with their spouse.
s00042Mr Alvin TanThese trends mean we need more homes than we did in the past, as the total number of households has increased.
s00043Mr Alvin TanMany Members on both sides of this House have also called for the relaxation of eligibility criteria to provide wider access to public housing and shorter waiting times for Build-To-Order (BTO) flats.
s00044Mr Alvin TanBut if we want more Singaporeans to qualify for HDB housing and to get their homes sooner, then we must build more homes and we must build them faster.
s00045Mr Alvin TanSo, the question, Mr Speaker, is not whether Singapore should continue to build homes, hospitals, schools and other developments to meet our people's needs.
s00046Mr Alvin TanThe question is where we build and how we build responsibly.
s00047Mr Alvin TanLet us go on next to where we build.
s00048Mr Alvin TanWe first ask a series of practical questions.
s00049Mr Alvin TanCan we make better use of existing land?
s00050Mr Alvin TanCan we build higher, go underground, bring compatible uses together, or better use under-utilised spaces?
s00051Mr Alvin TanThat is what we have been doing and we will continue to do.
s00052Mr Alvin TanFor example, relocating Paya Lebar Air Base to Changi and Tengah will free up a substantial area for redevelopment, as will consolidating our port activities at Tuas Port.
s00053Mr Alvin TanWe are also phasing out some golf courses and redeveloping older industrial areas for other uses.
s00054Mr Alvin TanWe are already redeveloping the former Keppel Golf Course as part of the Greater Southern Waterfront.
Section 6Golf course land redevelopment
s00055Mr Alvin TanBy 2030, we will have taken back more than 400 hectares of golf course land for redevelopment.
s00056Mr Alvin TanThis year, we announced Singapore's tallest public housing project – an over 60-storey development at Pearl's Hill.
s00057Mr Alvin TanRelaxing aviation height limits near airports also opens up new possibilities for us to build more intensely in suitable locations.
s00058Mr Alvin TanWe are developing rock caverns at Gali Batu, building on earlier projects such as the Jurong Rock Caverns.
s00059Mr Alvin TanAnd through the North-South Corridor, we are moving vehicular traffic underground, freeing surface space for walking, cycling and greenery.
s00060Mr Alvin TanWe are also doing more with existing sites and underused spaces, through integrated mixed-use developments, and by activating spaces beneath viaducts and on car park rooftops.
s00061Mr Alvin TanAs we do all this, we pay close attention to greenery and heritage.
s00062Mr Alvin TanToday, Singapore has about 7,800 hectares of green spaces, including our nature reserves.
s00063Mr Alvin TanEven after accounting for planned developments in the latest Master Plan, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) has safeguarded an additional 1,000 hectares of green space.
s00064Mr Alvin TanWe are also strengthening ecological connections between core habitats.
Section 7Restoring forest marine coastal habitats
s00065Mr Alvin TanBy 2030, we aim to restore and enhance 80 hectares of forest, marine and coastal habitats, and establish 300 kilometres of Nature Ways.
s00066Mr Alvin TanThese efforts help make Singapore one of the world's greenest high-density cities.
s00067Mr Alvin TanThe Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Green View Index found that Singapore is ahead of most cities in urban tree coverage, including cities with much lower population densities.
s00068Mr Alvin TanWe take a similar approach to heritage as well.
s00069Mr Alvin TanWe have conserved more than 7,200 buildings and structures in over 100 areas.
s00070Mr Alvin TanWhere possible, we retain significant heritage buildings and elements, and incorporate them into new developments.
s00071Mr Alvin TanThrough our Master Plan, we engage Singaporeans and set out how we use our limited land for the next 10 to 15 years.
s00072Mr Alvin TanAnd we review the Master Plan every five years through a major public consultation exercise, to ensure it remains relevant to our nation's changing needs.
s00073Mr Alvin TanA site's zoning reflects its long-term planning intention.
s00074Mr Alvin TanBut when we develop the site depends on our national needs, the availability of alternatives and if the supporting infrastructure is ready.
s00075Mr Alvin TanWithin this framework, we will always do our best to retain sites with significant greenery and heritage value.
s00076Mr Alvin TanBut there will be occasions when no other suitable site can meet the same need, in the same area and within the required timeframe.
s00077Mr Alvin TanAnd when that happens, we must weigh the trade-offs carefully and consider whether we can develop a site responsibly to meet an important national need, such as providing homes for Singaporeans.
s00078Mr Alvin TanWe proceed with great care when a site has significant ecological or heritage value.
s00079Mr Alvin TanGovernment agencies appoint independent external consultants to conduct an EIA or HIA, or both.
s00080Mr Alvin TanThese studies draw on inputs from nature and heritage groups.
s00081Mr Alvin TanFirst, they establish what is on the site today.
s00082Mr Alvin TanFor an EIA, this means identifying the site's important habitats, plants, animals and ecological connections.
s00083Mr Alvin TanFor a HIA, it means establishing the significance of the site's buildings, structures, landscape and other heritage attributes.
s00084Mr Alvin TanSecond, the consultants assess how the proposed development could affect these features.
s00085Mr Alvin TanAnd third, they recommend how to avoid, reduce or mitigate potential impact to the site.
s00086Mr Alvin TanDepending on the site, this could mean retaining areas of high ecological significance, maintaining ecological corridors, preserving important buildings or incorporating heritage elements into the new development.
s00087Mr Alvin TanFor an EIA, the consultants also propose a preliminary Environmental Management and Monitoring Plan (EMMP).
s00088Mr Alvin TanThe EMMP sets out mitigation measures, monitoring arrangements and reporting requirements that will apply during development.
s00089Mr Alvin TanSo, our general approach is to avoid impact where we can, reduce them where we cannot, and mitigate those that remain.
s00090Mr Alvin TanWe publish the findings, potential impact and proposed mitigation measures in the EIA or HIA report.
s00091Mr Alvin TanThis allows residents and the wider public to study the proposal and to give their feedback and views.
s00092Mr Alvin TanAgencies then consider the studies and feedback before finalising the detailed plans.
s00093Mr Alvin TanEIAs and HIAs are not meant to justify a detailed plan that is already fixed.
s00094Mr Alvin TanThey are an integral part of the consultation process through which the plan is shaped.
s00095Mr Alvin TanOnce development proceeds, HDB and the National Parks Board (NParks) will monitor the works and require contractors to provide regular updates, to ensure the measures are implemented properly.
Section 8Sunset Way housing planning intention
s00096Mr Alvin TanFor Sunset Way, the planning intention for housing had been reflected in the Master Plan since 1980.
s00097Mr Alvin TanThat intention has been reviewed and reaffirmed at each subsequent Master Plan review, including the most recent review in 2025.
s00098Mr Alvin TanFor Gillman Barracks, we announced the intention to study the site for development during the 2024 Committee of Supply debate.
s00099Mr Alvin TanThe site was subsequently rezoned to reflect that intention under Master Plan 2025.
s00100Mr Alvin TanBut we did not come to these sites first.
s00101Mr Alvin TanOver the years, we prioritised brownfield redevelopment in Clementi, Bukit Merah and surrounding areas.
s00102Mr Alvin TanIn Clementi and Bukit Merah, we redeveloped several older estates under the Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme.
s00103Mr Alvin TanIn Bukit Merah, we are redeveloping the former Keppel Golf Course, as I mentioned earlier.
s00104Mr Alvin TanBut demand for housing in these estates remains strong.
Section 9BTO launches oversubscribed
s00105Mr Alvin TanThe recent BTO launches at Clementi Emerald and Berlayar Rise were each oversubscribed by over four times.
s00106Mr Alvin TanMany Singaporeans, especially young families, want to continue living near their parents for mutual care and support.
s00107Mr Alvin TanMany understand this and so asked if we can build on sites that appear vacant or underused instead.
s00108Mr Alvin TanOne example is the former Raffles Junior College site at Mount Sinai where we are planning to introduce public housing in the near term, and the former bus facility at Ghim Moh where BTO construction is already in progress.
s00109Mr Alvin TanSome asked about the former Institute of Technical Education Headquarters site at the Dover-Medway area and a nearby site at Albert Winsemius Lane.
Section 10Housing redevelopment and Cross Island Line worksite
s00110Mr Alvin TanThe former will be redeveloped for a mix of public and private housing, to be launched over the next few years, and the latter is a Land Transport Authority (LTA) worksite that is needed to support ongoing works for the Cross Island Line.
s00111Mr Alvin TanIt will be considered for redevelopment in future after the Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) line is completed.
s00112Mr Alvin TanFor Gillman Barracks, some suggested building homes at Depot Lane Industrial Estate, the former Central Manpower Base (CMPB) and the "reserve site" at Pasir Panjang.
s00113Mr Alvin TanDepot Lane Industrial Estate is indeed part of our future housing supply and demolition of the buildings is currently ongoing to prepare the site.
s00114Mr Alvin TanWhile the former CMPB has moved out of Depot Road camp, the site is still required by the Ministry of Defence and other users.
s00115Mr Alvin TanThis also applies to the Pasir Panjang reserve site, where there are existing uses like the Ministry of Education Outdoor Adventure Learning Centre.
s00116Mr Alvin TanThis site can only be redeveloped in the longer term.
s00117Mr Alvin TanIn short, many of the sites suggested are already being developed for housing, are needed for other national purposes or cannot be redeveloped yet.
s00118Mr Alvin TanThat is why we need to develop Gillman Barracks and Sunset Way to meet our housing needs over the next decade.
Section 11Gillman Barracks environmental and heritage value
s00119Mr Alvin TanBut we recognise, Sir, that Gillman Barracks has both environmental and heritage value.
s00120Mr Alvin TanThat is why we commissioned the EIAs and HIA, because we assessed that the development could have significant environmental or heritage effects and wanted to carefully study the impact before finalising any plans.
s00121Mr Alvin TanThese are comprehensive reports, reflecting months of data collection and analysis by independent experts.
s00122Mr Alvin TanAt Gillman Barracks, we are studying how to retain most of the native-dominated secondary forest within the site.
s00123Mr Alvin TanWe are also studying how to maintain ecological connections in the East-West and North-South directions.
s00124Mr Alvin TanThe East-West connection would link Telok Blangah Hill Park and HortPark, and the North-South connection would comprise an ecological corridor, supporting the movement of birds towards Berlayar Creek and Labrador Nature Reserve.
Section 12Gillman Barracks heritage building retention
s00125Mr Alvin TanGillman Barracks also has a distinctive heritage character.
s00126Mr Alvin TanWe are thus studying the retention of all buildings assessed to be of "Exceptional" heritage significance, as well as most of those assessed to be of "High" heritage significance.
s00127Mr Alvin TanThis would allow the future neighbourhood to build on the character and charm of the former colonial buildings.
s00128Mr Alvin TanBut where a heritage building cannot be retained because of practical site constraints, we will explore other ways to preserve its history.
s00129Mr Alvin TanThese include detailed documentation, salvaging and reusing suitable materials, and incorporating heritage interpretation into the future development.
s00130Mr Alvin TanAt Sunset Way, we are studying the retention of a significant stretch of greenery along the former Jurong Railway Line.
s00131Mr Alvin TanThis would preserve an important part of our railway heritage while maintaining ecological connectivity within the site.
s00132Mr Alvin TanWe are also studying the retention of a natural stream and its surrounding riparian buffer, which provides refuge for wildlife.
s00133Mr Alvin TanThese retained green areas will be supplemented with more native trees, and serving as buffers between the future neighbourhood and existing residential estates.
s00134Mr Alvin TanOur approach to both sites will be informed by science and evidence.
s00135Mr Alvin TanGillman Barracks and Sunset Way lie within the wider Labrador Nature Park and Clementi Nature Corridor respectively, as NParks identified through its ecological profiling exercise.
s00136Mr Alvin TanThe proposed retention areas are based on findings of the environmental studies, that aim to maintain ecological connectivity across these wider landscapes.
s00137Mr Alvin TanHDB will also study how to design these future neighbourhoods to reduce urban heat.
s00138Mr Alvin TanThis includes using environmental modelling to improve wind flow, incorporating greenery, using cool-paint and orientating residential blocks to minimise direct sun exposure.
Section 13Housing plan and green heritage areas
s00139Mr Alvin TanWe are not yet able to give an exact figure because the layout, scale and detailed design have not yet been finalised.
s00140Mr Alvin TanBut in our current conceptual plan, we already reduced the number of homes to retain important green and heritage areas identified through the studies.
s00141Mr Alvin TanIf we conserve even more, we will build even fewer homes.
s00142Mr Alvin TanSo, we must weigh this trade-off carefully before reading a final decision.
s00143Mr Alvin TanHDB has also been attending local grassroots advisers' dialogues with residents to hear their concerns and suggestions in person.
s00144Mr Alvin TanWe appreciate the time and effort that many have put into studying the reports, attending dialogues and submitting detailed feedback.
s00145Mr Alvin TanI personally engaged many stakeholders myself and walked the ground at both Sunset Way and Gillman.
s00146Mr Alvin TanYoung People's Action Party (PAP) and PAP Sustainability Group have also conducted engagements, gathering feedback and sharing that feedback with me and my team.
s00147Mr Alvin TanSome nature enthusiasts, heritage advocates and nearby residents also asked us to preserve more greenery and heritage.
s00148Mr Alvin TanAt the same time, we also heard from many Singaporeans, including residents in Clementi and Telok Blangah, about their desire for more affordable and accessible public housing.
s00149Mr Alvin TanMany tell us they hope their children will have an opportunity to live near them.
Section 14Consultation period and development plans
s00150Mr Alvin TanAfter the formal consultation period closes on 6 August 2026, we will conduct further engagements with stakeholders and closely review the study findings and feedback we received before finalising our detailed development plans.
s00151Mr Alvin TanWe will also publish a report summarising agencies' responses to the feedback and any amendments made to the original set of plans.
s00152Mr Alvin TanThe challenge is how we balance these needs responsibly within our limited space.
s00153Mr Alvin TanWe will and must always make the best use of existing land and safeguard our most important natural and heritage assets.
s00154Mr Alvin TanBut there will be times where we cannot avoid difficult trade-offs.
s00155Mr Alvin TanWhen that happens, we must be clear about why we need to build, deliberate about where we build and take great care over how we build.
s00156Mr Alvin TanWe must be honest with Singaporeans about the choices before us, listen carefully to their views and improve our plans wherever we can.
s00157Mr Alvin TanAnd after weighing all these different considerations, Government must decide in the best interests of Singapore and Singaporeans.
s00158Mr Alvin TanThis is the approach we are taking for Gillman Barracks and Sunset Way.
s00159Mr Alvin TanWe are studying the environmental and heritage findings, listening to public views and examining how the proposals can be improved before the detailed plans are finalised.
s00160Mr Alvin TanAnd they will continue to confront us as we build homes, strengthen our economy, expand our infrastructure and realise our vision of a City in Nature.
s00161Mr Alvin TanThey made them with courage and foresight, and Singapore is now better for it.
Section 15Leaving a greener country for children
s00162Mr Alvin TanOur responsibility is to do the same – so that we can leave to our children a country that is greener, more liveable and continues to provide opportunities and good homes for our people.
s00163Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)These came from in-person meetings, community sessions and written feedback, including well-researched proposals that the residents put together themselves.
s00164Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)I understand and appreciate the stated need for more housing and the potential benefits for many families.
s00165Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)Along these considerations, my residents have also raised deep concerns including the loss of biodiversity and ecological connectivity in the area, the loss of the very greenery that drew many residents to make this precinct to their home.
s00166Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)For many, Gillman Forest is a place of respite, reflection and connection.
s00167Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)Also raised is the impact on climate resilience and urban heat.
s00168Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)With that, I would like to ask four supplementary questions.
s00169Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)First, can the Government clarify whether, and if so how, the earlier Berlayer EIA informed the Gillman Barracks EIA, particularly in relation to ecological connectivity corridor design and the cumulative impact across the two adjacent developments?
s00170Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)Residents have raised concerns over developing Berlayer and Gillman Barracks in close succession, particularly since both sides form part of the same ecological network and serve the same wildlife.
s00171Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)In this context, they have asked why the recommended ecological widths differ between the two, despite this shared ecology.
s00172Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)The Gillman Forest links the Southern Ridges, which includes the Telok Blangah Hill Park, Berlayer Creek through to Labrador Nature Reserve and Kent Ridge Park, forming a larger ecological landscape.
s00173Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)Retaining it alongside shared residents, would also honour Singapore's 2021 pledge under the Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use to halt and reverse forest loss by 2030.
s00174Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)My second supplementary question: instead of residential development on Gillman Barracks, will the Government consider re-imagining and re-engineering the site to better meet the evolving needs of our next generation, creating spaces that protect and promote human creativity and connection?
s00175Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)My third supplementary question: will the Government review our planning and consultation processes to ensure they remain fit for purpose in the changing climate, specifically for forested or ecologically sensitive sites, could EIAs and public engagement begin at the master planning stage before land is slated for development?
s00176Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)My final supplementary question: will the Government provide a summary of the feedback collected, together with clarity on how it shaped the final development decisions?
s00177Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)This matters deeply to residents, who want assurance that their voices have made a difference.
Section 16Plans for Sunset Way and Gillman Barracks
s00178Mr Alvin TanAs I mentioned earlier on, the plans for both Sunset Way, and in this case, Gillman Barracks are not yet finalised.
s00179Mr Alvin TanEven beyond 6 August, when the consultation period closes, we will continue to engage her residents.
s00180Mr Alvin TanAnd after this further engagement and reviewing the feedback and findings from additional engagements with the residents, we will release reports summarising the responses to feedback and also any adjustments that we make to the original set of plans.
s00181Mr Alvin TanWith regards to the Gillman EIA and its links to Berlayer, the Gillman EIA took into consideration the Berlayer Estate.
s00182Mr Alvin TanIt has established an important connectivity, in fact, between Gillman and Berlayer for the movement of birds.
s00183Mr Alvin TanAnd these draw upon the findings from the NParks' ecological profiling exercise, which I mentioned earlier on, and the Keppel Club EIA.
s00184Mr Alvin TanAnd the conceptual plan, therefore proposes retaining the East-West Corridor, as I mentioned earlier on, and to establish a new North-South Corridor, to facilitate the movement of fauna.
Section 17Ecological corridor width proposals
s00185Mr Alvin TanBoth studies also proposed a minimum 30-metre ecological corridor, and for Gillman Barracks, its recommended corridor stretches up to 200 metres.
s00186Mr Alvin TanSo, we acknowledge that there is ecological connectivity between sites, we have done that through the EIAs and the EIAs for each site is different because each site is unique, but where possible, we recognise the connectivity.
s00187Mr Alvin TanOn building on new spaces within this site, as I have mentioned, we will take in those feedback in the consultation process, even beyond 6 August.
s00188Mr Alvin TanWe will listen to residents and see where we can make adjustments.
Section 18Singapore green spaces and nature reserves
s00189Mr Alvin TanOn the spaces which the Member has mentioned, as I have mentioned, today, Singapore has over 7,800 hectares of green spaces and nature reserves.
s00190Mr Alvin TanAnd if you look at the bigger picture, even after accounting for the planned developments in both sites in the Master Plan, URA has safeguarded an additional 1,000 hectares of green space.
s00191Mr Alvin TanSo, net-net, we are building a green city.
s00192Mr Alvin TanAll of these plans, be it in Sunset Way or Gillman, are meant to enhance that ecological connectivity and also to balance between development for homes, as well as green and heritage places.
s00193Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)I have three supplementary questions for you today.
s00194Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)The second supplementary question is, the Minister of State referred to quite a number of significant initiatives to free up further brownfield land, such as the relocation of Paya Lebar Air Base, the continuing relocation of our port terminals to Tuas, as well as taking back golf course land.
s00195Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)Will enough of the brownfield land be freed up in time, so that we can continue to defer the development of green spaces like Maju Forest and Gillman Forest?
s00196Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)And my third supplementary question is regarding the location of the Cross Island Line Maju Station, does the Government regard the location of Maju Station as compelling or requiring the development of Maju Forest, in order to be able to sufficiently utilise the capacity that the station will provide?
Section 19MRT planning and ecological sites
s00197Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)And if that being the case, will the Government consider in the future, when planning MRT lines, alignments and station locations, that we take into account the location of sensitive, ecological sites, such as Maju Forest, such that we do not perpetuate a vicious cycle where this station is planned for that location and therefore, it compels development of the forest?
s00198Mr Alvin TanI made it quite clear that the sites that we mentioned earlier on – Sunset Way as well as Gillman Barracks – have already been zoned for residential use under our Master Plan and they have been set aside for housing.
s00199Mr Alvin TanSo, we will proceed, but how we build is important.
s00200Mr Alvin TanAnd that is why we have these EIAs and HIA to identify the ecological significance, the heritage significance, and then, we will mitigate as best as possible, the ecological and heritage impact to the sites.
s00201Mr Alvin TanWith regard to alternatives, I mentioned earlier on that we have looked in the vicinity of both Sunset Way as well as Gillman Barracks for alternative sites – vacant land, brownfield sites, underused sites.

How to read it. Left is the record itself: sentences the model kept are in full ink with a green edge, sentences pulled in only so a kept sentence has its antecedent are mid-grey, and everything the model passed over is faint. Flip the switch to drop the faint ones and the record collapses to the selection — nothing is deleted, it is just out of the way.

Why the summaries move. An earlier version put the summaries in their own column aligned to the passages they covered, with braces drawn across. It failed: with 40 sentences of record collapsing to 8 kept ones, no two things could be lined up, and the braces crossed each other. Keeping the summaries in a rail that follows the reader removes the alignment problem instead of solving it — the summary arrives when its section does.

The right panel is model-written, and that is the one place this page can be wrong. Three rounds of prompt rules did not reduce the rate at which the model adds a specific the source does not state, so the summary is treated as a derived convenience rather than evidence. Everything checkable is on the left, in the record's own words. If a summary disagrees with the passage beside it, the passage is right.
